prompt: Force a single bit of an int to 1 with setBit, or to 0 with clearBit, using shifted masks with the | and & operators.
explanation: ORing with a mask that has a single 1 forces that bit to 1 while leaving every other bit alone, because x | 0 is x. Clearing uses the opposite trick: ~(1 << bit) is a mask of all 1s except a single 0, and ANDing with it forces just that bit to 0, because x & 1 is x. Both operations are idempotent -- setting an already-set bit or clearing an already-clear bit changes nothing.
hints: Build the mask the same way for both methods: int mask = 1 << bit;
setBit: value | mask -- OR with 0 leaves bits alone, OR with 1 forces a 1.
clearBit: value & ~mask -- ~ flips the mask to all 1s with one 0, and AND keeps every bit except that one.
